definitions.gloss: self-serving; drawing water to one's own rice field
definitions.explanation: Acting in one's own interest; interpreting situations to one's own advantage; being self-serving in arguments or actions.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{意見|いけん}は{我田引水|がでんいんすい}だ。
{我田引水|がでんいんすい}な{解釈|かいしゃく}をしないでほしい。
examples.english: Please don't interpret things to suit your own interests.

examples.japanese: その{論文|ろんぶん}は{我田引水|がでんいんすい}な{主張|しゅちょう}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: That paper has many self-serving arguments.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {我|が} (my/one's own) + {田|でん} (rice field) + {引|いん} (draw/pull) + {水|すい} (water). The image is of a farmer diverting irrigation water to their own field, leaving less for neighbors.

USAGE: Used to criticize someone for being self-serving, biased, or interpreting facts to favor themselves. Often used as a na-adjective.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{我田引水|がでんいんすい}な{意見|いけん} (a self-serving opinion)
・{我田引水|がでんいんすい}な{解釈|かいしゃく} (a self-serving interpretation)
・{我田引水|がでんいんすい}に{考|かんが}える (to think in a self-serving way)

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・{自分勝手|じぶんかって} (selfish)
・{手前味噌|てまえみそ} (self-praise, tooting one's own horn)
・{利己的|りこてき} (selfish, egotistical)
